heading: INT. CHURCH BASEMENT - AA MEETING - NIGHT

units.text: INT. CHURCH BASEMENT - AA MEETING - NIGHT
Folding chairs in a circle.
A coffee urn on a card table.
A banner reading ONE DAY AT A TIME hangs crooked over a stack of Christmas decorations.
DR. PHILLIPA ROSS, 40s, hospital lanyard still around her neck, sits across from DENNIS CAHILL, 60s, an ex-paramedic in a cardigan too warm for the room.
Hi, I'm Dennis, and I'm an alcoholic.
units.name: DENNIS
paren: raising his paper cup, to the empty chairs

units.text: Hi, Dennis.
units.name: PHILLIPA

units.text: Phillipa, we're the only two people here. You can skip the choir response.
units.name: DENNIS

units.text: I like to keep my form.
units.name: PHILLIPA

units.text: A door SLAMS upstairs.
They both look at the ceiling.
Dennis counts to three on his fingers.
That's the bingo group. They're worse than we are.
units.name: DENNIS

units.text: Dennis. Can I tell you something, as a doctor and not as a drunk?
units.name: PHILLIPA

units.text: Please. I've been hoping someone would finally diagnose me.
units.name: DENNIS

units.text: I operated on a man this morning. Thirty-eight. He had a bad liver and a good laugh. He said, Doctor, I'm going to quit. I said, you'd better. And then I came here and sat in a car for forty minutes because I wanted a drink more than I've ever wanted anything.
units.name: PHILLIPA

units.text: Did you go in the bar?
units.name: DENNIS

units.text: I came here. I came here and I'm telling you I'm scared. She is not supposed to be scared. She is supposed to be the one holding the scalpel.
units.name: PHILLIPA

units.text: Dennis looks at her.
He does not say it is fine.
The urn GURGLES.
She's allowed. So is he. So are you.
units.name: DENNIS

units.text: Dennis. You used three pronouns.
units.name: PHILLIPA

units.text: I contain multitudes. And a lot of decaf.
units.name: DENNIS

units.text: The phone on the card table BUZZES.
Phillipa glances at it.
Her face goes still.
It's the hospital. They need me back.
units.name: PHILLIPA

units.text: Then go. Come back next week and tell me how it went.
units.name: DENNIS
paren: standing, offering his cardigan, as if it were a medal

units.text: It smells like a library.
units.name: PHILLIPA

units.text: It smells like twenty-six months.
units.name: DENNIS

units.text: She nods.
She puts it on over her scrubs.
Upstairs, somebody shouts BINGO and the whole ceiling rattles.
